Heard on admission.
Trial Court record perused.
Prima facie, this appeal seems to be arguable.
Hence, admitted for final hearing.

Further heard on I.A. No.32519/2024, which is a first application under Section 389(1) of the CrPC,
1973 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 03.09.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012), Raisen (M.P.) in SC No.17 of 2022,
whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 366 and 376(2)(n) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 -10 years and fine of Rs.1,000/- for each offence with default stipulations.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant that prosecutrix is not found by the learned trial Court less than 18 years of age.
2 CRA-12094-2024

sentences.text: She was major.
As per the story of prosecution, she remained missing on 22.5.2022 and she has been recovered on 24.5.2022.
In between this period, she remained with the present appellant but didn't oppose the appellant and didn't inform anyone who were residing nearby and the persons available during the travelling.
It is revealed from the statement of prosecutrix (P.W.1) in para 15 that she has given the statement to the police that she likes the present appellant and wants to marry him.

It is also admitted by her in para 20 and 21 that where they happened to be stayed in Bhopal, the persons were residing nearby in huts and she was remained alone during day time but she has not communicated anyone residing nearby about the incident and that the present appellant has committed forceful rape on her.
She has traveled through bus from Bhopal to Raisen but inbetween this travelling she has not informed any person travelling in the bus.

1 be major is indicative of consensual relationship between the parties.

sentences.text: Therefore, no case is made out.
In view of the contradictions and variations in the statements of the prosecution witnesses, coupled with the inherent infirmities in the prosecution case, the appellant has a good case on merits.
The present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
Looking to the period of custody, benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted and the appellant may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A.
No.32519/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail.
The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 03.08.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE mrs. mishra Raj @ Halke vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49953335/
